samples.reference_class: Emerging infectious diseases in the Americas
drivers_up: Oropouche virus was identified as causing large outbreaks in endemic areas and new areas in South America.
Cuba reported its first confirmed case in June 2024, indicating spread to new territories.
There were already 7 countries reporting cases in 2024, suggesting a rising trend.
drivers_down: The disease may be contained through public health interventions, limiting its spread to new countries.
Oropouche virus is primarily vector-borne, which may limit its spread to areas with suitable vectors.
samples.why_might_be_wrong: The spread of the Oropouche virus could be underestimated if there are unreported cases or if new regions become endemic faster than anticipated.
samples.rationale: The evidence indicates a trend of increasing spread, with new territories like Cuba reporting their first cases and existing endemic areas experiencing large outbreaks. However, the spread is also constrained by factors like vector presence and potential public health interventions. Given the information, it is reasonable to expect moderate to significant spread, aligning with the 9 to 11 range as the most likely outcome.
